title.zh: 卷二百五十九 列傳第十八 張美 郭守文 尹崇珂 劉廷讓 袁繼忠 崔彥進 張廷翰 皇甫繼明 張瓊
title.en: Volume 259 Biographies 18: Zhang Mei, Guo Shuowen, Yin Chongke, Liu Tingrang, Yuan Jizhong, Cui Yanjin, Zhang Tinghan, Huangfu Jiming, Zhangg Qiong
title.raw: 卷二百五十九 列傳第十八 張美 郭守文 尹崇珂 劉廷讓 袁繼忠 崔彥進 張廷翰 皇甫繼明 張瓊 Volume 259 Biographies 18: Zhang Mei, Guo Shuowen, Yin Chongke, Liu Tingrang, Yuan Jizhong, Cui Yanjin, Zhang Tinghan, Huangfu Jiming, Zhangg Qiong

sentences.zh: 張美，字玄珪，貝州清河人。

translations.literal: Zhang Mei, styled Xuangui, was a man of Qinghe in Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mei, whose style was Xuangui, came from Qinghe in Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 少善書計，初為左藏小吏，以彊幹聞。

translations.literal: In youth he was skilled at writing and reckoning; he first served as a minor clerk in the Left Repository and became known for forceful competence.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was adept at accounts and records; he began as a junior clerk in the Left Repository and won a reputation for vigorous efficiency.

sentences.zh: 三司薦奏，特補本庫專知，出為澶州糧料使。

translations.literal: The Three Departments recommended him in memorial; he was specially appointed specialist of his own depot and went out as grain commissioner of Chunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On recommendation from the Three Departments he was specially made specialist of his depot, then sent out as Chunzhou grain commissioner.

sentences.zh: 周世宗鎮澶淵，每有求取，美必曲為供給。

translations.literal: When the Later Zhou Shizong held Chanyuan, whenever he made requests, Mei invariably bent rules to supply him.
translations.idiomatic: While the Later Zhou Shizong was posted at Chanyuan, Zhang Mei would contrive to meet every request the prince made.

sentences.zh: 周祖聞之怒，將譴責之，而恐傷世宗意，徙美為濮州馬步軍都虞候。

translations.literal: The Zhou founder heard of it and was angry; he was about to reprimand him, yet feared wounding the Shizong's feelings, and transferred Mei to be chief adjutant of Puzhou horse-and-foot forces.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou founder was furious when he heard of this and meant to punish Mei, but fearing to offend the Shizong he instead transferred him to chief adjutant of the Puzhou combined forces.

sentences.zh: 四年，世宗再幸淮上，皆為大內都點檢。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when the Shizong again visited the Huai region, [Mei] each time served as grand inspector of the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, on the Shizong's second tour of the Huai, Mei served each time as grand inspector of the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 北征，又為大內都部署。

translations.literal: On the northern campaign he again became grand deployer of the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: During the northern expedition he was again made grand deployer of the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 師還，為左監門衛上將軍，充宣徽北院使，判三司。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he became senior general of the Left Gate Guard, acting as commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, and concurrently directed the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: After the army came home he was made senior general of the Left Gate Guard, commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, and put in charge of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 美彊力有心計，周知其利病，每有所條奏釐革，上多可之，常以幹敏稱。

translations.literal: Mei was forceful and resourceful, thoroughly knowing what was profitable and harmful; whenever he submitted proposals for reform, the ruler mostly approved them, and he was commonly praised for competence and quickness.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mei was forceful and shrewd; he knew every gain and loss in the accounts, and most of his reform memorials won approval. He was widely known for administrative sharpness.

sentences.zh: 世宗連歲征討，糧饋不乏，深委賴焉。

translations.literal: The Shizong campaigned year after year, yet grain supplies never fell short; he deeply relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Through years of the Shizong's campaigns supplies never ran short, and the emperor placed deep trust in him.

sentences.zh: 然以澶淵有所求假，頗薄之，美亦自愧。

translations.literal: Yet because of requests and loans at Chanyuan, [the Shizong] rather looked down on him, and Mei also felt ashamed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Still, remembering the favors Mei had shown him at Chanyuan, the Shizong held him somewhat cheap, and Mei himself was ashamed.

sentences.zh: 恭帝嗣位，加檢校太傅。

translations.literal: When the Gong Emperor succeeded, he was given the additional title of Grand Tutor with inspection.
translations.idiomatic: When the Gong Emperor came to the throne, Mei was given the honorary rank of Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 宋初，加檢校太尉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was given the additional title of Grand Commandant with inspection.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he was made honorary Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 初，李筠鎮上黨，募亡命，多為不法，漸倔彊難制。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Yun held Shangdang; he recruited fugitives, many of whom acted unlawfully, and gradually grew defiant and hard to control.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Li Yun held Shangdang, he recruited fugitives who committed many outrages and grew steadily more defiant and hard to control.

sentences.zh: 美度筠必叛，陰積粟於懷、孟間。

translations.literal: Mei judged that Yun would surely rebel and secretly stored grain between Huai and Meng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mei foresaw that Li Yun would rebel and quietly stockpiled grain between Huai and Meng.

sentences.zh: 後筠果叛，太祖親討之，大軍十萬出太行，經費無闕，美有力焉。

translations.literal: Later Yun did rebel; Taizu personally campaigned against him; a great army of one hundred thousand issued through Taihang, and funds and supplies were not lacking—Mei had strength in this.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yun did rebel, Taizu led the campaign in person; a hundred thousand men marched through Taihang without want of funds or supplies, and Zhang Mei had much to do with it.

sentences.zh: 拜定國軍節度。

translations.literal: He was appointed military commissioner of Dingguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed military commissioner of the Dingguo circuit.

sentences.zh: 縣官市木關中，同州歲出緡錢數十萬以假民，長吏十取其一，謂之率分錢，歲至數百萬，美獨不取。

translations.literal: When the government bought timber in Guanzhong, Tongzhou each year issued several hundred thousand strings of cash to lend the people; senior officials took one in ten, called "apportionment money," reaching several million per year—Mei alone did not take it.
translations.idiomatic: When the state bought timber in Guanzhong, Tongzhou each year lent the people several hundred thousand strings of cash; local heads took a ten-percent cut called apportionment money, amounting yearly to millions—but Zhang Mei alone refused his share.

sentences.zh: 未幾，他郡有詣闕訴長吏受率分錢者，皆命償之。

translations.literal: Before long, in other prefectures there were those who came to court accusing senior officials of receiving apportionment money; all were ordered to make restitution.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward officials from other prefectures came to court accusing their superiors of taking apportionment money, and the throne ordered every offender to repay it.

sentences.zh: 乾德五年，移鎮滄州。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qiande he was transferred to hold Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiande 5 he was transferred to Cangzhou as military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初來朝，改左驍衛上將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he came to court and was changed to senior general of the Left Valiant Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taiping Xingguo he came to court and was made senior general of the Left Valiant Guard.

sentences.zh: 美獻都城西河曲灣果園二、蔬圃六、亭舍六十餘區。

translations.literal: Mei presented two orchards at Hequwan west of the capital, six vegetable gardens, and more than sixty pavilions and lodges.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mei presented two orchards at Hequwan west of the capital, six vegetable gardens, and more than sixty pavilions and lodges.

sentences.zh: 八年，請老，以本官致仕。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he requested retirement and left office with his original rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he asked to retire and left office with his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，卒，年六十八。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi he died, aged sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yongxi 2, at the age of sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 淳化初，諡恭惠。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chunhua he was given the posthumous title Gonghui.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chunhua he was posthumously titled Gonghui.

sentences.zh: 子守瑛，至供備庫使。

translations.literal: His son Shouying rose to commissioner of the Supply Repository.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shouying rose to commissioner of the Supply Repository.

sentences.zh: 孫士宗，至內殿承制。

translations.literal: His grandson Shizong rose to inner-hall director.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Shizong rose to inner-hall director.

sentences.zh: 士宗卒，士禹為崇班，士安至閤門祗候，士宣為禮賓副使。

translations.literal: When Shizong died, Shiyu became a court gentleman; Shi'an rose to gate attendant; Shixuan became vice commissioner of ceremonial guests.
translations.idiomatic: After Shizong's death, Shiyu became a court gentleman, Shi'an a gate attendant, and Shixuan vice commissioner of ceremonial guests.

sentences.zh: 郭守文

translations.literal: Guo Shouwen
translations.idiomatic: Guo Shouwen

sentences.zh: 郭守文，幷州太原人。

translations.literal: Guo Shouwen was a man of Taiyuan in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Shouwen came from Taiyuan in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 父暉，仕漢為護聖軍使，從周祖征河中，戰死。

translations.literal: His father Hui served Han as commissioner of the Imperial Guard Army; following the Zhou founder's campaign in Hezhong, he died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hui had served the Han as commissioner of the Imperial Guard; he followed the Zhou founder against Hezhong and was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 守文年十四，居喪哀毀，周祖憐之，召隸帳下。

translations.literal: Shouwen was fourteen; in mourning he was so grief-stricken he wasted away; the Zhou founder pitied him and summoned him to serve under his banner.
translations.idiomatic: Shouwen was only fourteen; in mourning he grieved himself nearly to death, and the Zhou founder, taking pity, brought him into his personal service.

sentences.zh: 廣順初，補左班殿直，再遷東第二班副都知。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun he was appointed left-rank palace attendant; he was twice promoted to deputy chief of the eastern second rank.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guangshun he was made a left-rank palace attendant and soon promoted twice to deputy chief of the eastern second rank.

sentences.zh: 宋初，遷西頭供奉官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was transferred to western-head tribute commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he was made western-head tribute commissioner.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，遷知簡州。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified, he was transferred to administer Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu was pacified he was put in charge of Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 時劍外多寇，守文悉招來集附。

translations.literal: At the time beyond Jian there were many bandits; Shouwen entirely summoned them to come and attach themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits were numerous beyond the passes; Shouwen summoned them all in and won their submission.

sentences.zh: 從潘美征嶺南，會擒劉鋹，遣守文馳傳告捷，遷翰林副使。

translations.literal: Following Pan Mei in the campaign in Lingnan, when Liu Chang was captured, he sent Shouwen by rapid relay to announce victory; he was transferred to vice commissioner of the Hanlin.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Pan Mei into Lingnan; when Liu Chang was taken, Shouwen was sent by express relay to report the victory and was promoted to Hanlin vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 從曹彬等平金陵，護送李煜歸闕下。

translations.literal: Following Cao Bin and others in pacifying Jinling, he escorted Li Yu back to the court.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Cao Bin and others in taking Jinling and escorted Li Yu to the capital.

sentences.zh: 時煜以拒命頗自歉，不欲生見太祖。

translations.literal: At the time Yu, because of resisting orders, was rather ashamed himself and did not wish to see Taizu alive.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu, ashamed of having resisted the throne, did not wish to face Taizu alive.

sentences.zh: 守文察知之，因謂煜曰：「國家止務恢復疆土，以致太平，豈復有後至之責耶？

translations.literal: Shouwen perceived this and therefore said to Yu: "The state only strives to recover territory and bring peace—how could there still be blame for coming late?
translations.idiomatic: Shouwen saw his fear and told him, "The court seeks only to recover the realm and secure peace—why should there be blame for submitting late?

sentences.zh: 」煜心遂安。

translations.literal: " Yu's heart then grew calm.
translations.idiomatic: " At that Li Yu's mind was eased.

sentences.zh: 改西京作坊使、領翰林司事。

translations.literal: He was changed to commissioner of the western capital workshops and directed Hanlin affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was made commissioner of the western capital workshops and put in charge of Hanlin affairs.

sentences.zh: 俄從党進破並寇於團柏谷。

translations.literal: Soon he followed Dang Jin in defeating Bing raiders at Tuanbogu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he followed Dang Jin in defeating Bing raiders at Tuanbogu.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，秦州內附，蕃部騷動，命守文乘傳撫諭，西夏悅伏。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo, when Qinzhou submitted inward, frontier tribes were unsettled; he was ordered to travel by relay to soothe and instruct them, and the Western Xia gladly submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taiping Xingguo, when Qinzhou came over, frontier tribes grew restless; Shouwen was sent by express to reassure them, and the Western Xia submitted willingly.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷西上閤門使。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to western upper gate commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made western upper gate commissioner.

sentences.zh: 是夏，汴水決於寧陵，發宋、亳丁壯四千五百塞之，命守文董其役。

translations.literal: That summer the Bian River burst at Ningling; four thousand five hundred able-bodied men of Song and Bo were mobilized to block it, and Shouwen was ordered to supervise the work.
translations.idiomatic: That summer the Bian burst at Ningling; forty-five hundred laborers from Song and Bo were drafted to stem it, and Shouwen was ordered to oversee the work.

sentences.zh: 是冬，又與閤門副使王侁、西八作副使石全振護塞靈河縣決河。

translations.literal: That winter, together with vice gate commissioner Wang Yan and western workshops vice commissioner Shi Quanzhen, he guarded and blocked the breach at Linghe county.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he joined vice gate commissioner Wang Yan and western workshops vice commissioner Shi Quanzhen in sealing the breach at Linghe.

sentences.zh: 及征太原，守文與判四方館事梁迥分護行營馬步軍。

translations.literal: When they campaigned against Taiyuan, Shouwen and Liang Jiong, who judged affairs of the Four Directions Hall, separately guarded the campaign horse-and-foot forces.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taiyuan campaign, Shouwen and Liang Jiong of the Four Directions Hall each took charge of the field army's horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 會劉繼元降，其弟繼文據代州，依遼人之援以拒命，遣守文討平之。

translations.literal: When Liu Jiyuan surrendered, his younger brother Jiwen held Daizhou, relying on Liao aid to resist orders; Shouwen was sent to suppress and pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jiyuan surrendered, his brother Jiwen held Daizhou with Liao support and refused obedience; Shouwen was sent to crush him.

sentences.zh: 俄受詔護定州屯兵，大破遼人於蒲城。

translations.literal: Soon he received orders to guard the garrison at Dingzhou and greatly defeated the Liao at Pucheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to command the Dingzhou garrison and routed the Liao at Pucheng.

sentences.zh: 以功遷東上閤門使、領澶州刺史。

translations.literal: For merit he was transferred to eastern upper gate commissioner and concurrently held Chunzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was made eastern upper gate commissioner and prefect of Chunzhou.

sentences.zh: 召還，擢拜內客省使。

translations.literal: Recalled, he was promoted and appointed commissioner of the Inner Guests Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he was promoted to commissioner of the Inner Guests Bureau.

sentences.zh: 八年，滑州房村河決，發卒塞之，命守文董其役。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Fangcun River at Huazhou burst; troops were mobilized to block it, and Shouwen was ordered to supervise the work.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the Fangcun River at Huazhou burst; troops were sent to dam it, and Shouwen was again put in charge.

sentences.zh: 遼人擾雄州，命守文率禁兵數萬人赴援，既至，遼人遁去。

translations.literal: The Liao harassed Xiongzhou; Shouwen was ordered to lead several tens of thousands of imperial troops to relieve it; once he arrived, the Liao fled.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liao raided Xiongzhou, Shouwen led tens of thousands of imperial guards to the relief; the Liao withdrew as soon as he arrived.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，詔守文率兵屯三交，俄加領武州團練使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi an edict ordered Shouwen to lead troops and garrison Sanjiao; soon he was additionally made regimental trainer of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi 2 he was ordered to garrison Sanjiao with his troops and soon given the concurrent post of regimental trainer of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 屬夏人擾攘，命守文帥師討之，破夏州鹽城鎮岌羅膩等十四族，斬首數千級，俘獲生畜萬計。

translations.literal: As the Xia people were in turmoil, he was ordered to command troops against them; he broke fourteen tribes including Jiluoni of Yancheng town in Xiazhou, beheaded several thousand, and captured livestock by the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tangut frontier erupted, Shouwen led the campaign, crushing fourteen tribes including Jiluoni of Yancheng in Xiazhou, taking several thousand heads and vast herds of livestock.

sentences.zh: 又破咩嵬族，殲焉。

translations.literal: He again broke the Miewei tribe and annihilated them.
translations.idiomatic: He also destroyed the Miewei tribe to the last man.

sentences.zh: 諸部畏懼，相率來降，凡銀、麟、夏三州歸附者百二十五族、萬六千餘戶，西鄙遂寧。

translations.literal: The various tribes feared and came in succession to surrender; in all, of Yin, Lin, and Xia three prefectures, one hundred twenty-five tribes and more than sixteen thousand households submitted, and the western border was then tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Tribes across the west submitted in fear; one hundred twenty-five clans and more than sixteen thousand households of Yin, Lin, and Xia came over, and the frontier was quiet.

sentences.zh: 五年春，大舉北伐，為幽州道行營前軍步軍水陸都監。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year a great northern expedition was launched; he became overall inspector of foot forces, water, and land of the vanguard on the Youzhou route.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifth year, during the great northern expedition, he was made overall inspector of the Youzhou vanguard's foot, river, and land forces.

sentences.zh: 卒與遼人遇，為流矢所中，氣色不撓，督戰益急，軍中服其量。

translations.literal: He suddenly met the Liao, was struck by a stray arrow, yet his bearing did not falter; he urged battle all the more urgently, and the army admired his fortitude.
translations.idiomatic: He suddenly met the Liao and took a stray arrow, yet his bearing never faltered; he pressed the fight harder still, and the army admired his nerve.

sentences.zh: 會大軍不利，坐違詔逗遛退軍，左遷右屯衛大將軍。

translations.literal: As the great army fared badly, he was punished for violating the edict by lingering and withdrawing; he was demoted to great general of the Right Garrison Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the main force failed, he was punished for disobeying orders by lingering on the retreat and was demoted to great general of the Right Garrison Guard.

sentences.zh: 事具《曹彬傳》。

translations.literal: The affair is fully set forth in the biography of Cao Bin.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in the biography of Cao Bin.

sentences.zh: 明年復舊職，裁三月，拜宣徽北院使。

translations.literal: The next year he was restored to his former post; after only three months he was appointed commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was restored to his former post; three months later he was made commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 又與田欽祚並為北面排陣使，屯鎮州。

translations.literal: He was also together with Tian Qinzuo made northern array commissioners and garrisoned Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He and Tian Qinzuo were jointly made northern array commissioners and stationed at Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，改南院使、鎮州路都部署。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong he was changed to southern bureau commissioner and overall deployer of the Zhenzhou circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Duangong he was made southern bureau commissioner and overall deployer of the Zhenzhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 又為北面行營都部署兼鎮定、高陽關兩路排陣使。

translations.literal: He was again made overall deployer of the northern campaign headquarters and concurrently array commissioner of the Zhending and Gaoyang Pass circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made overall deployer of the northern headquarters and array commissioner for the Zhending and Gaoyang Pass circuits.

sentences.zh: 是冬，遼騎南侵，大破之唐河。

translations.literal: That winter Liao horsemen invaded south; he greatly defeated them at the Tang River.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, when Liao cavalry raided south, he routed them on the Tang River.

sentences.zh: 端拱三年十月，卒，年五十五。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year of Duangong he died, aged fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth month of Duangong 3, at the age of fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 太宗悼惜之，贈侍中。

translations.literal: Taizong mourned and cherished his memory, posthumously granting him Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong mourned him deeply and posthumously made him Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 諡忠武，追封譙王，遣中使護喪，歸葬京師。

translations.literal: He was given the posthumous title Zhongwu, enfeoffed posthumously as Prince of Qiao, and a palace envoy was sent to escort the funeral; he was buried in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Zhongwu and enfeoffed as Prince of Qiao; a palace envoy escorted the funeral home for burial in the capital.

sentences.zh: 守文沈厚有謀略，頗知書，每朝退，習書百行，出言溫雅，未嘗忤人意。

translations.literal: Shouwen was deep, steady, and resourceful, quite learned in books; after each court session he practiced one hundred lines of writing; his words were mild and elegant, and he never offended people's feelings.
translations.idiomatic: Shouwen was grave, thoughtful, and well read; after every court session he copied a hundred lines, spoke with mild grace, and never gave offense.

sentences.zh: 先是，將臣戍邊者多致寇以邀戰功，河朔諸州殆無寧歲，既敗岐溝關，乃命守文以內職總兵鎮常山以經略之。

translations.literal: Earlier, generals guarding the frontier often provoked raiders to seek battle merit; the Hebei prefectures scarcely had a peaceful year; after defeat at Qiguguan, Shouwen was ordered with an inner-office post to command troops and hold Changshan to manage the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, frontier commanders had often provoked raids to win glory, and Hebei knew scarcely a quiet year; after Qiguguan, Shouwen was sent with an inner-office post to command at Changshan and steady the north.

sentences.zh: 守文既喪月餘，中使自北邊來言：「守文死，軍士皆流涕。

translations.literal: More than a month after Shouwen's death, a palace envoy came from the northern border saying: "Shouwen is dead, and the soldiers all weep.
translations.idiomatic: More than a month after Shouwen died, a palace envoy from the north reported, "Since Shouwen's death the soldiers have wept.

sentences.zh: 」帝問：「何以得此？

translations.literal: " The Emperor asked: "How could he win this?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor asked, "How did he earn that?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「守文得奉祿賜賚悉犒勞士卒，死之日，家無餘財。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Shouwen took all salary and gifts to reward the troops; on the day he died his house had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "Shouwen gave every stipend and gift to his men; when he died his household had nothing left.

sentences.zh: 」帝嗟歎久之，賜其家錢五百萬，為真宗納其女為夫人，即章穆皇后也。

translations.literal: " The Emperor sighed long, granted his family five million in cash, and had Zhenzong take his daughter as consort—she was Empress Zhangmu.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor sighed at length, gave the family five million cash, and had Zhenzong marry his daughter, who became Empress Zhangmu.

sentences.zh: 子崇德，至太子中舍；

translations.literal: His son Chongde rose to middle aide of the heir apparent;
translations.idiomatic: His son Chongde rose to middle aide of the heir apparent;

sentences.zh: 崇信，至西京左藏庫使、同知皇城司，贈福州觀察使；

translations.literal: Chongxin rose to western-capital Left Repository commissioner and associate director of the Imperial City Bureau, posthumously granted Fuzhou observation commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: Chongxin rose to western-capital Left Repository commissioner and associate director of the Imperial City Bureau, and was posthumously made observation commissioner of Fuzhou;

sentences.zh: 崇儼至崇儀使、全州刺史，贈潤州觀察使。

translations.literal: Chongyan rose to ceremonial commissioner and Quanzhou prefect, posthumously granted Runzhou observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyan rose to ceremonial commissioner and prefect of Quanzhou, and was posthumously made observation commissioner of Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 諸司使無廢朝、贈官之例，崇信、崇儼咸以后兄故，特示優禮。

translations.literal: Commissioners of the various bureaus had no precedent for court mourning or posthumous offices; Chongxin and Chongyan, both as brothers-in-law of the empress, were specially shown favor.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau commissioners were not normally granted court mourning or posthumous offices; Chongxin and Chongyan, as the empress's brothers, received exceptional honors.

sentences.zh: 崇德子承壽，至虞部員外郎。

translations.literal: Chongde's son Shoushou rose to outer aide of the Works Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Chongde's son Shoushou rose to outer aide of the Works Bureau.

sentences.zh: 天禧五年，錄承壽子若水為太常寺奉禮郎，崇仁為解州團練使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianxi, Shoushou's son Ruoshui was enrolled as ceremonial attendant of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Chongren as regimental trainer of Jiezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianxi 5, Shoushou's son Ruoshui was enrolled as a ceremonial attendant of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Chongren as regimental trainer of Jiezhou.

sentences.zh: 尹崇珂

translations.literal: Yin Chongke
translations.idiomatic: Yin Chongke

sentences.zh: 宋初，出為淄州刺史，有善政，民詣闕請刻石頌德，太祖命殿中侍御史李穆撰文賜之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he went out as Zizhou prefect; he had good government; the people came to court requesting a stone inscription praising his virtue, and Taizu ordered Palace Attendant Censor Li Mu to compose the text and grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he was sent out as prefect of Zi; his rule was benevolent, and the people petitioned the court for a stone inscription in his praise; Taizu had Palace Attendant Censor Li Mu compose the text.

sentences.zh: 討湖南，為行營前軍馬軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: In the campaign against Hunan he was commander of the vanguard horse forces of the campaign headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the Hunan campaign he commanded the vanguard horse of the field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 荊湘平，授朗州團練使。

translations.literal: When Jing and Xiang were pacified, he was appointed regimental trainer of Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing and Xiang were pacified, he was made regimental trainer of Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 又與潘美、丁德裕克郴州。

translations.literal: He again, with Pan Mei and Ding Deyu, captured Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Pan Mei and Ding Deyu in taking Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 乾德中，征嶺表，以崇珂為行營馬步軍副部署。

translations.literal: In Qiande, campaigning in Lingbiao, Chongke was made deputy deployer of campaign horse-and-foot forces.
translations.idiomatic: During Qiande, in the Lingnan campaign, Chongke was made deputy deployer of the field army's horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 克廣州，擒劉鋹，即日詔與潘美同知廣州兼市舶轉運等使，錄功遷保信軍節度。

translations.literal: When Guangzhou was taken and Liu Chang captured, that same day an edict made him and Pan Mei jointly administer Guangzhou and concurrently maritime trade and transport commissioner; for recorded merit he was transferred to military commissioner of Baoxin Army.
translations.idiomatic: After Guangzhou fell and Liu Chang was taken, he and Pan Mei were that day made joint administrators of Guangzhou and maritime trade commissioners; for his merit he was made military commissioner of Baoxin.

sentences.zh: 未幾，南漢開府樂範、容州都指揮使鄧存忠、韶州賊帥周思瓊、春恩道都指揮使麥漢瓊等據五州之地以叛。

translations.literal: Before long, Southern Han grand councilor Le Fan, Rongzhou commander Deng Cunzhong, Shaozhou bandit chief Zhou Siqiong, Chun'en circuit commander Mai Hanqiong, and others held five prefectures in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Le Fan of the Southern Han court, Rongzhou commander Deng Cunzhong, Shaozhou rebel Zhou Siqiong, Chun'en commander Mai Hanqiong, and others seized five prefectures and rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 崇珂討之，太祖遣中使李神祐督戰，數月盡平其黨，還治所。

translations.literal: Chongke campaigned against them; Taizu sent palace envoy Li Shenyou to supervise battle; in several months their faction was entirely pacified, and he returned to his seat of government.
translations.idiomatic: Chongke suppressed them; Taizu sent palace envoy Li Shenyou to oversee the fighting; within months the rebels were crushed, and he returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 六年，卒，年四十二。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he died, aged forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year, at the age of forty-two.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 遣中使護其喪，歸葬洛陽。

translations.literal: A palace envoy was sent to escort his funeral; he was buried in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: A palace envoy escorted the funeral home for burial in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 以其子昭吉、弟崇珪並為西京作坊使，昭吉領會州刺史，崇珪領歙州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Zhaoji and younger brother Chonggui were both made western-capital workshop commissioners; Zhaoji concurrently held Huizhou prefect and Chonggui Shezhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhaoji and brother Chonggui were both made western-capital workshop commissioners; Zhaoji was also prefect of Hui and Chonggui of She.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗在周朝娶崇珂妹，追諡淑德皇后。

translations.literal: Earlier, Taizong in the Zhou dynasty married Chongke's younger sister; she was posthumously titled Empress Shude.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while still in the Zhou, Taizong had married Chongke's sister, later posthumously titled Empress Shude.

sentences.zh: 昭吉至洛苑使。

translations.literal: Zhaoji rose to commissioner of the Luoyang park.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoji rose to commissioner of the Luoyang park.

sentences.zh: 次子昭輯，至供奉官、閤閣門祗候。

translations.literal: The second son Zhaoji rose to tribute commissioner and gate attendant of the Inner Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The second son, Zhaoji, rose to tribute commissioner and inner gate attendant.

sentences.zh: 劉廷讓

translations.literal: Liu Tingrang
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tingrang

sentences.zh: 劉廷讓，字光乂，其先涿州范陽人。

translations.literal: Liu Tingrang, styled Guangyi, his ancestors were men of Fanyang in Zhuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tingrang, whose style was Guangyi, came of Fanyang stock in Zhuozhou.

sentences.zh: 曾祖仁恭，唐盧龍軍節度。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Rengong was military commissioner of the Tang Lulong Army.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Rengong had been military commissioner of the Tang Lulong Army.

sentences.zh: 祖守文，襲滄州盧彥威，遂據其城，昭宗授以節鉞。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shouwen attacked Lu Yanwei of Cangzhou, seized his city, and Emperor Zhaozong invested him with command seal and axe.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shouwen attacked Lu Yanwei at Cangzhou, took the city, and Emperor Zhaozong invested him with the seal and axe of command.

sentences.zh: 後其弟守光囚父仁恭，守文舉兵討之，軍敗，為守光所殺。

translations.literal: Later his younger brother Shouguang imprisoned their father Rengong; Shouwen raised troops to punish him, was defeated in battle, and was killed by Shouguang.
translations.idiomatic: Later his younger brother Shouguang imprisoned their father Rengong; Shouwen raised an army against him, was defeated, and was killed by Shouguang.

sentences.zh: 廷讓與其父延進避難南奔。

translations.literal: Tingrang and his father Yanjin fled south to escape the turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Tingrang and his father Yanjin fled south to escape the fighting.

sentences.zh: 少有膂力，周祖鎮鄴，以隸帳下。

translations.literal: In youth he had strong physique; when the Zhou founder held Ye, he was assigned to serve under his banner.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was powerfully built; when the Zhou founder held Ye, he was brought into his personal service.

sentences.zh: 廣順初，補內殿直押班，累遷龍捷都校。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun he was appointed inner-hall direct escort squad leader; through repeated promotions he became chief commander of the Dragon Rapid Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guangshun he was made an inner-hall direct escort squad leader and rose through repeated promotions to chief commander of the Dragon Rapid Guard.

sentences.zh: 從世宗征淮南，以功領雷州刺史。

translations.literal: Following Shizong's campaign in the Huai region, for merit he was given Leizhou as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Shizong against the Huai region and, for his achievements, was given Leizhou as prefect.

sentences.zh: 再遷涪州團練使、領鐵騎右廂。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to regimental trainer of Fuzhou and concurrently held the right wing of the Iron Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was next made regimental trainer of Fuzhou and given command of the right wing of the Iron Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 宋初，轉江州防禦使、領龍捷右廂。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was transferred to defense commissioner of Jiangzhou and concurrently held the right wing of the Dragon Rapid Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he became defense commissioner of Jiangzhou and commander of the right wing of the Dragon Rapid Guard.

sentences.zh: 從征李筠，為行營先鋒使。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Li Yun, he served as vanguard commissioner of the field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the campaign against Li Yun as vanguard commissioner of the field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年，改侍衛馬軍都指揮使、領江寧軍節度。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianlong he was changed to commander-in-chief of the Palace Cavalry Guard and concurrently military commissioner of the Jiangning Army.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianlong 2 he was made commander-in-chief of the Palace Cavalry Guard and military commissioner of the Jiangning Army.

sentences.zh: 乾德二年春，詔領兵赴潞州，以備幷寇。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Qiande, an edict ordered him to lead troops to Luzhou to guard against Bing invaders.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Qiande 2 he was ordered to lead troops to Luzhou to guard against raids from Bing.

sentences.zh: 冬，興師伐蜀，為四川行營前軍兵馬副都部署，率禁兵步騎萬人、諸州兵萬人，由歸州進討。

translations.literal: In winter, when armies were raised to attack Shu, he became deputy overall deployer of vanguard forces of the Sichuan expedition headquarters, leading ten thousand imperial foot and horse and ten thousand troops from various prefectures, advancing by way of Guizhou to attack.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, when armies marched against Shu, he was made deputy overall deployer of the Sichuan expedition's vanguard and led ten thousand imperial foot and horse plus ten thousand troops from the prefectures, advancing through Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 入其境，連破松木、三會、巫山等砦，獲蜀將南光海等五千餘人，擒戰棹都指揮使袁德宏等千二百人，奪戰艦二百餘艘。

translations.literal: Upon entering Shu territory, he successively captured the forts of Songmu, Sanhui, Wushan, and others, taking more than five thousand Shu soldiers including the general Nanguang Hai, capturing more than twelve hundred including Yuan Dehong, commander of battle boats, and seizing more than two hundred warships.
translations.idiomatic: Once inside Shu, he took the forts at Songmu, Sanhui, Wushan, and elsewhere in succession, capturing more than five thousand Shu troops including General Nanguang Hai, more than twelve hundred men including Yuan Dehong, commander of the battle boats, and over two hundred warships.

sentences.zh: 又獲水軍三千人，因度南岸，斬三千餘級。

translations.literal: He also captured three thousand naval troops; crossing to the south bank, he beheaded more than three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He also took three thousand naval troops, crossed to the south bank, and beheaded more than three thousand men.

sentences.zh: 初，夔州有鎖鏁江為浮梁，上設敵棚三重，夾江列礮具。

translations.literal: Earlier, at Kuizhou a chain had been stretched across the river as a floating bridge, with three tiers of enemy barricades above it and siege engines lined up along both banks.
translations.idiomatic: At Kuizhou the Shu had chained the river into a floating bridge, set three tiers of battle platforms above it, and lined both banks with artillery.

sentences.zh: 廷讓等將行，太祖以地圖示之，指鏁江曰：「我軍至此，泝流而上，慎勿以舟師爭勝，當先以步騎陸行，出其不意擊之，俟其勢卻，即以戰棹夾攻，取之必矣。

translations.literal: When Tingrang and the others were about to set out, Taizu showed them a map, pointed to the chained river, and said: "When our army reaches this point and moves upstream, take care not to contest victory with the navy; you should first march by land with foot and horse, strike with surprise, and once their force withdraws, use battle boats to attack from both sides — you are sure to take it.
translations.idiomatic: Before Tingrang and his colleagues set out, Taizu showed them a map, pointed to the chained river, and said: "When our army reaches this point and moves upstream, do not try to win with the fleet. March first by land with foot and horse, strike by surprise, and once they fall back, send the battle boats in from both sides — you are sure to take it.

sentences.zh: 」及師至，距鏁江三十里，舍舟步進，先奪其橋，復牽舟而上，破州城，守將高彥儔自焚，悉如太祖計。

translations.literal: When the army arrived, thirty li from the chained river they abandoned their boats and advanced on foot, first seizing the bridge, then hauling boats upstream, broke the prefecture city; the defending general Gao Yanchou burned himself — all exactly as Taizu had planned.
translations.idiomatic: When the army arrived, thirty li short of the chained river, they left their boats and marched overland, seized the bridge first, then hauled their boats upstream, and broke the prefecture city; the defending general Gao Yanchou burned himself to death — all exactly as Taizu had planned.

sentences.zh: 遂進克萬、施、開、忠四州，峽中郡縣悉下。

translations.literal: They then advanced and captured Wan, Shi, Kai, and Zhong — four prefectures — and all counties in the gorges submitted.
translations.idiomatic: They then took Wan, Shi, Kai, and Zhong — four prefectures — and all the counties in the gorges fell.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，次遂州，州將陳俞率吏民來降。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year they halted at Suizhou; the prefect Chen Yu led officials and people to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year they reached Suizhou, where Prefect Chen Yu led officials and commoners in surrender.

sentences.zh: 盡出府庫金帛以給將士。

translations.literal: He emptied the treasury's gold and silks to pay the troops.
translations.idiomatic: He emptied the treasury of gold and silks to pay the soldiers.

sentences.zh: 初出師也，太祖命之曰：「所得郡縣，當傾帑藏，為朕賞戰士，國家所收唯土疆爾。

translations.literal: When the army first set out, Taizu had ordered them: "In every prefecture and county you take, empty the treasuries to reward my warriors for me; what the state receives is only the territory.
translations.idiomatic: When the army first marched, Taizu had ordered: "In every prefecture and county you capture, empty the treasuries to reward my warriors; all the state keeps is the land itself.

sentences.zh: 」故人皆效命，所至成功。

translations.literal: Therefore everyone gave their utmost, and wherever they went they succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Men gave their utmost everywhere, and success followed wherever they went.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，王全斌等皆坐縱部下掠奪子女玉帛及納賄賂左降，惟廷讓秋毫無犯。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified, Wang Quanbin and the others were all punished for letting their subordinates plunder women, children, jade, and silks and for accepting bribes and demoted in rank; only Tingrang did not violate so much as a hair's breadth.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu was pacified, Wang Quanbin and the others were all punished and demoted for letting their men plunder people, jade, and silks and for taking bribes; only Tingrang had not touched so much as a hair.

sentences.zh: 及全師雄等作亂，郡縣相應，寇盜蠭起。

translations.literal: When Quan Shixiong and others rose in revolt, prefectures and counties responded in turn, and bandits swarmed like bees.
translations.idiomatic: When Quan Shixiong and others rebelled, prefectures and counties rose in response, and bandits swarmed everywhere.

sentences.zh: 廷讓又與曹彬破之，以功改領鎮安軍節度，從征太原。

translations.literal: Tingrang again, together with Cao Bin, defeated them; for merit he was changed to hold the military commission of the Zhen'an Army and followed the campaign against Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Tingrang again joined Cao Bin in crushing them, was rewarded with the military commission of the Zhen'an Army, and followed the campaign against Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 開寶六年，出為鎮寧軍節度。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kaibao he went out as military commissioner of the Zhenning Army.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaibao 6 he was sent out as military commissioner of the Zhenning Army.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，入為右驍衛上將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo he came to court as senior general of the Right Valiant Cavalry Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 2 he returned to court as senior general of the Right Valiant Cavalry Guard.

sentences.zh: 雍熙三年，曹彬敗於岐溝關，諸將失律，多坐黜免。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi, Cao Bin was defeated at Qiguguan; the generals violated discipline, and many were dismissed and demoted.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi 3, Cao Bin was defeated at Qiguguan; the generals had broken discipline, and many were dismissed or demoted.

sentences.zh: 既而契丹擾邊，時議遣將，無愜上意者。

translations.literal: Then the Khitan harassed the frontier; when the court debated sending a general, none pleased the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Khitan raided the frontier; when the court debated whom to send, no candidate satisfied the emperor.

sentences.zh: 時廷讓與宋偓、張永德並罷節鎮在環列，帝欲令擊契丹自效，乃遣分守邊郡，以廷讓知雄州，又徙瀛州兵馬都部署。

translations.literal: At the time Tingrang, together with Song Wo and Zhang Yongde, had all been removed from military commissions and were attending at court in the circling ranks; the emperor wished to have them strike the Khitan to redeem themselves, so he sent them to hold border prefectures separately — Tingrang to administer Xiongzhou, and then transferred as overall deployer of Yingzhou's troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Tingrang, Song Wo, and Zhang Yongde had all been stripped of their military commissions and were attending at court; the emperor wanted them to redeem themselves against the Khitan, so he sent them to separate border posts — Tingrang to Xiongzhou, then as overall deployer of Yingzhou's forces.

sentences.zh: 是冬，契丹數萬騎來侵，廷讓與戰君子館。

translations.literal: That winter, tens of thousands of Khitan horsemen came raiding; Tingrang fought them at Junzi Lodge.
translations.idiomatic: That winter tens of thousands of Khitan horsemen invaded, and Tingrang met them at Junzi Lodge.

sentences.zh: 時天大寒，兵士弓弩皆不能彀，契丹圍廷讓數重。

translations.literal: The weather was bitterly cold; the soldiers' bows and crossbows could not be drawn, and the Khitan encircled Tingrang layer upon layer.
translations.idiomatic: The cold was extreme; the men's bows and crossbows would not draw, and the Khitan surrounded Tingrang in ring after ring.

sentences.zh: 廷讓先分精兵屬李繼隆為後殿，緩急為援。

translations.literal: Tingrang had earlier detached elite troops under Li Jilong as rearguard to aid in any emergency.
translations.idiomatic: Tingrang had earlier set aside elite troops under Li Jilong as rearguard to support him in any crisis.

sentences.zh: 至是，繼隆退保樂壽，廷讓一軍皆沒，死者數萬人，僅以數騎獲免。

translations.literal: At this point Jilong withdrew to hold Leshou; Tingrang's entire army was wiped out — tens of thousands died, and he escaped with only a few horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: At that point Jilong fell back to Leshou; Tingrang's whole army was destroyed — tens of thousands died, and he escaped with only a handful of horsemen.

sentences.zh: 先鋒將賀令圖、楊重進皆陷於契丹。

translations.literal: The vanguard generals He Lingtu and Yang Chongjin both fell into Khitan hands.
translations.idiomatic: The vanguard generals He Lingtu and Yang Chongjin both fell into Khitan hands.

sentences.zh: 自是河朔戍兵無鬥志，又科鄉民為兵以守城，皆未習戰鬥。

translations.literal: From then on the garrison troops of Hebei lost fighting spirit; moreover conscripted villagers were made soldiers to hold the cities, and none were trained for battle.
translations.idiomatic: After that the Hebei garrisons lost their will to fight; villagers were conscripted to hold the cities, and none of them knew war.

sentences.zh: 契丹遂長驅而入，陷深、祁、德數州，殺官吏，俘士民，所在輦金帛而去。

translations.literal: The Khitan then drove deep inland, capturing several prefectures including Shen, Qi, and De, killing officials, taking common people captive, and wherever they went carting off gold and silks.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan then drove deep into the country, taking Shen, Qi, De, and other prefectures, killing officials, seizing the people, and carting off gold and silks wherever they went.

sentences.zh: 博、魏之北，民尤苦焉。

translations.literal: North of Bo and Wei the people suffered especially.
translations.idiomatic: North of Bo and Wei the people suffered most of all.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞之，下哀痛之詔。

translations.literal: When Taizong heard of it, he issued an edict of grief and anguish.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong heard of it, he issued an edict of mourning and grief.

sentences.zh: 初，廷讓詣闕待罪，太宗知為李繼隆所誤，不之責。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Tingrang came to court to await punishment, Taizong knew he had been misled by Li Jilong and did not blame him.
translations.idiomatic: When Tingrang first came to court to accept blame, Taizong knew Li Jilong had misled him and did not hold him responsible.

sentences.zh: 四年，復命代張永德知雄州兼兵馬部署。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was again appointed to replace Zhang Yongde as administrator of Xiongzhou and concurrent troops-and-horses deployer.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was again appointed to replace Zhang Yongde as administrator of Xiongzhou and overall deployer of its forces.

sentences.zh: 是秋以疾聞，帝遣內醫診視，因上言求歸京師，不俟報，乃離屯所。

translations.literal: That autumn illness was reported; the emperor sent a palace physician to examine him; he thereupon memorialized requesting return to the capital, and without waiting for a reply left his garrison post.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn his illness was reported; the emperor sent a palace physician to examine him, and he memorialized asking to return to the capital; without waiting for a reply he left his post.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，下御史按問，獄具。

translations.literal: The emperor was furious and ordered the censorate to investigate; the case was established.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and ordered the censorate to investigate; the case was proved.

sentences.zh: 下詔曰：「右驍衛上將軍劉廷讓，朕以其宿舊，曾董軍政，擢自環尹，付之成師，俾控邊關，式防寇鈔。

translations.literal: An edict was issued: "Senior General of the Right Valiant Cavalry Guard Liu Tingrang — We, considering his long service, once entrusted him with overall military administration, raised him from attendance at court, gave him command of a formed army, charged him with controlling the border passes and guarding against raiders.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Senior General of the Right Valiant Cavalry Guard Liu Tingrang — We, considering his long service, once put him in charge of military affairs, raised him from attendance at court, gave him a formed army, and charged him with holding the border passes and guarding against raids.

sentences.zh: 而乃以病為解，不俟報命，委棄戎重，俶裝上道。

translations.literal: Yet he took illness as his excuse, did not await Our reply, abandoned a weighty military post, packed up, and took to the road.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he pleaded illness, did not await Our reply, abandoned a vital military post, packed up, and set out on the road.

sentences.zh: 矧萬旅所集，實制於中權，列燧相望，或虞於外侮。

translations.literal: Moreover, where tens of thousands of troops are assembled, the central authority in truth holds command; beacon-fires stand in sight of one another, yet there may be fear of external aggression.
translations.idiomatic: Where tens of thousands of troops are gathered, central command in truth holds sway; beacon-fires stand within sight of one another, yet the frontier may still fear attack.

sentences.zh: 事機一失，咎責安歸？

translations.literal: Once the moment is lost, to whom shall blame fall?
translations.idiomatic: Once the moment is lost, upon whom shall blame fall?

sentences.zh: 有司議刑，當在不赦。

translations.literal: The judicial officers recommend punishment; it should be beyond pardon.
translations.idiomatic: The judicial officers recommend punishment that should not be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 錄其素效，特從寬典，可削奪在身官爵，配隸商州。

translations.literal: Recording his past merits, We specially apply lenient measures: he is stripped of all offices and ranks he holds and is assigned to Shangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Recording his past service, We apply lenient measures: he is stripped of all offices and ranks he holds and is assigned to Shangzhou.

sentences.zh: 」又黜其子如京使永德為濠州團練副使，崇儀副使永和為唐州刺史。

translations.literal: Also his son Yongde, a palace envoy, was demoted to vice regimental trainer of Haozhou; and Yonghe, a vice commissioner of the Imperial Insignia Office, to prefect of Tangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yongde, a palace envoy, was also demoted to vice regimental trainer of Haozhou, and Yonghe, a vice commissioner of the Imperial Insignia Office, to prefect of Tangzhou.

sentences.zh: 廷讓既黜，怏怏不食，行至華州卒，年五十九。

translations.literal: After Tingrang was dismissed, resentful and refusing food, he died en route at Huazhou, aged fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: After his dismissal Tingrang brooded and refused food; he died on the road at Huazhou, aged fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 帝錄其舊勳，贈太師。

translations.literal: The emperor recorded his old merit and posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor recorded his old service and posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 子永德，至內殿崇班；

translations.literal: His son Yongde rose to inner-hall court gentleman;
translations.idiomatic: His son Yongde rose to inner-hall court gentleman;

sentences.zh: 永恭，至西京作坊副使；

translations.literal: Yonggong rose to vice commissioner of the Western Capital workshop;
translations.idiomatic: Yonggong rose to vice commissioner of the Western Capital workshop;

sentences.zh: 永和，為內殿承制；

translations.literal: Yonghe became inner-hall director;
translations.idiomatic: Yonghe became inner-hall director;

sentences.zh: 永錫，至崇班；

translations.literal: Yongxi rose to court gentleman;
translations.idiomatic: Yongxi rose to court gentleman;

sentences.zh: 永保、永昌、永規並至閤門祗候；

translations.literal: Yongbao, Yongchang, and Yonggui all rose to gate attendants;
translations.idiomatic: Yongbao, Yongchang, and Yonggui all rose to gate attendants;

sentences.zh: 永崇，為崇班；

translations.literal: Yongchong became a court gentleman;
translations.idiomatic: Yongchong became a court gentleman;

sentences.zh: 永寧及孫允忠並為閤門祗候。

translations.literal: Yongning and his grandson Yunzhong both became gate attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Yongning and his grandson Yunzhong both became gate attendants.

sentences.zh: 袁繼忠

translations.literal: Yuan Jizhong
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Jizhong

sentences.zh: 袁繼忠，其先振武人，後徙幷州。

translations.literal: Yuan Jizhong — his ancestors were from Zhenwu; later they moved to Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Jizhong came of Zhenwu stock; his family later moved to Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 父進，仕周為階州防禦使。

translations.literal: His father Jin served Zhou as defense commissioner of Jiezhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jin had served the Zhou as defense commissioner of Jiezhou.

sentences.zh: 繼忠以父任補右班殿直。

translations.literal: Jizhong entered service through his father's appointment as right-rank palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhong entered service through his father's rank and was made a right-rank palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 太祖平澤、潞，討幷、汾，悉預攻戰。

translations.literal: When Taizu pacified Ze and Lu and attacked Bing and Fen, Jizhong took part in all the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu pacified Ze and Lu and attacked Bing and Fen, Jizhong fought in every campaign.

sentences.zh: 乾德中征蜀，隸大將劉廷讓麾下。

translations.literal: In the Qiande campaign against Shu he served under the great general Liu Tingrang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qiande campaign against Shu he served under the great general Liu Tingrang.

sentences.zh: 既克蜀，知雲安軍，歷嘉、蜀二州監軍。

translations.literal: After Shu was captured he was made military prefect of Yun'an and successively military supervisor of Jia and Shu prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu fell he was put in charge of Yun'an Army and served successively as military supervisor of Jia and Shu prefectures.

sentences.zh: 開寶中伐廣南，為先鋒壕砦。

translations.literal: In Kaibao he campaigned against Guangnan as vanguard trench-and-fort builder.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaibao he campaigned against Guangnan as vanguard in building trenches and forts.

sentences.zh: 廣南平，以功遷供奉官，護隰州白壁關屯兵。

translations.literal: When Guangnan was pacified, for merit he was promoted to tribute commissioner and guarded the garrison troops at Baiqi Pass, Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangnan was pacified he was promoted to tribute commissioner for his achievements and put in charge of the garrison at Baiqi Pass in Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 時河東拒命，繼忠累入其境，破三砦，擒將校二人，得生口、馬牛羊、鎧仗逾萬計。

translations.literal: At the time Hedong defied orders; Jizhong repeatedly entered their territory, captured three forts, seized two officers, and took captives, horses, cattle, sheep, armor, and weapons numbering more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When Hedong defied the court, Jizhong repeatedly raided its territory, took three forts, captured two officers, and seized captives, livestock, armor, and weapons by the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 近戍主將懼無功受譴，以誠告繼忠，繼忠以所獲分與之，遂與都巡檢郭進略地忻、代州，改天平軍巡檢。

translations.literal: The nearby garrison commander feared being punished for lack of achievement and told Jizhong honestly; Jizhong divided what he had captured and gave it to him, then together with overall inspector Guo Jin raided the territory of Xin and Dai prefectures; he was changed to inspector of the Ping'an Army.
translations.idiomatic: The local garrison commander feared punishment for having achieved nothing and confessed as much to Jizhong; Jizhong shared his spoils with him, then joined overall inspector Guo Jin in raiding Xin and Dai prefectures, and was made inspector of the Ping'an Army.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，以為閤門祗候，令擊梅山洞賊，破之。

translations.literal: When Taizong acceded, Jizhong was made a gate attendant and ordered to attack the bandits of Meishan Cave; he defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong came to the throne, Jizhong was made a gate attendant and ordered against the bandits of Meishan Cave; he defeated them.

sentences.zh: 又巡遏邊部於唐龍鎮。

translations.literal: He also patrolled and held the frontier sector at Tanglong garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He also patrolled and held the frontier at Tanglong garrison.

sentences.zh: 太宗征太原，繼忠預破鷹揚軍，先登陷陣。

translations.literal: When Taizong campaigned against Taiyuan, Jizhong beforehand broke the Yingyang Army, was first to scale the walls and smash the enemy formation.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong campaigned against Taiyuan, Jizhong first broke the Yingyang Army, was first over the wall, and smashed the enemy line.

sentences.zh: 契丹入代境，繼忠率兵擊走之。

translations.literal: When the Khitan entered Dai territory, Jizhong led troops and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan entered Dai territory, Jizhong led troops and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 以功遷通事舍人，護高陽關屯兵。

translations.literal: For merit he was promoted to courier of affairs and guarded the garrison troops at Gaoyang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was promoted to courier of affairs and put in charge of the garrison at Gaoyang Pass.

sentences.zh: 與崔彥進破契丹長城口，殺獲數萬眾，璽書褒美。

translations.literal: Together with Cui Yanjin he broke the Khitan at Changcheng Pass, killing and capturing tens of thousands; an imperial letter praised him.
translations.idiomatic: With Cui Yanjin he routed the Khitan at Changcheng Pass, killing and capturing tens of thousands, and received an imperial letter of praise.

sentences.zh: 時有勸繼忠自論其功者，繼忠不答。

translations.literal: At the time some urged Jizhong to petition on his own behalf about his achievements; Jizhong did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Jizhong to petition on his own behalf about his achievements; he did not respond.

sentences.zh: 會趙保忠來朝獻其地，綏州刺史李克憲偃蹇不奉詔，遣繼忠諭旨，竟率克憲入朝。

translations.literal: When Zhao Baozhong came to court offering his territory, Suizhou prefect Li Kezian was arrogant and would not obey the edict; Jizhong was sent to convey the imperial will and in the end led Kezian to court.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Baozhong came to court offering his territory, Suizhou Prefect Li Kezian was defiant and refused the edict; Jizhong was sent to convey the imperial will and in the end brought Kezian to court.

sentences.zh: 遷西上閤門副使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice commissioner of the Western Upper Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice commissioner of the Western Upper Gate.

sentences.zh: 詔與田仁朗率兵定河西諸州，大破西人於葭蘆州，遷引進副使，護定州屯兵。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him together with Tian Renlang to lead troops to pacify the prefectures of the Hexi; they greatly defeated the westerners at Jialu Prefecture; he was promoted to vice introducing commissioner and guarded the garrison troops at Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered with Tian Renlang to lead troops in pacifying the Hexi prefectures; they routed the westerners at Jialu Prefecture; he was promoted to vice introducing commissioner and put in charge of the garrison at Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，遷西上閤門使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi he was promoted to commissioner of the Western Upper Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi 2 he was promoted to commissioner of the Western Upper Gate.

sentences.zh: 三年，大將田重進征契丹，命繼忠為定州路行營馬步軍都監。

translations.literal: In the third year the great general Tian Chongjin campaigned against the Khitan; Jizhong was appointed overall inspector of horse and foot forces on the Dingzhou route expedition headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the great general Tian Chongjin campaigned against the Khitan, and Jizhong was made overall inspector of horse and foot forces on the Dingzhou route expedition headquarters.

sentences.zh: 領師取飛狐，下靈丘，平蔚州，擒其帥大鵬翼以獻，事見《重進傳》。

translations.literal: Leading the army he took Feihu, captured Lingqiu, pacified Yuzhou, and captured its commander Da Pengyi to present; the matter is set forth in the biography of Tian Chongjin.
translations.idiomatic: He led the army in taking Feihu, capturing Lingqiu, pacifying Yuzhou, and presenting the captured commander Da Pengyi — the full account appears in the biography of Tian Chongjin.

sentences.zh: 師還，繼忠為後殿，行列甚整。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Jizhong served as rearguard; the ranks were very orderly.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march Jizhong commanded the rearguard, and the ranks were perfectly ordered.

sentences.zh: 至定州，重進欲斬降卒後期至者，繼忠諭以殺降不祥，皆救免之。

translations.literal: Reaching Dingzhou, Chongjin wished to execute surrendered soldiers who arrived late; Jizhong admonished him that killing captives was inauspicious, and all were spared.
translations.idiomatic: At Dingzhou, Chongjin wanted to execute surrendered soldiers who had arrived late; Jizhong warned that killing captives was ill-omened, and all were spared.

sentences.zh: 遷判四方館事、領播州刺史，護屯兵如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to judge affairs of the Four Directions Hall and concurrently given Bozhou as prefect, guarding garrison troops as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was made judge of affairs of the Four Directions Hall and given Bozhou as prefect, while continuing to command the garrison troops as before.

sentences.zh: 大將李繼隆以易州靜塞騎兵尤驍果，取隸麾下，畜其妻子城中。

translations.literal: The great general Li Jilong took the Jingse cavalry of Yizhou, who were especially fierce and bold, and attached them to his own command, keeping their wives and children in the city.
translations.idiomatic: The great general Li Jilong took the Jingse cavalry of Yizhou, who were especially fierce and bold, into his own command and kept their wives and children in the city.

sentences.zh: 繼忠言於繼隆曰：「此精卒，止可守城，萬一敵至，城中誰與悍者？

translations.literal: Jizhong said to Jilong: "These are elite troops — they can only be used to hold the city; if the enemy should come, who in the city will fight alongside the brave?
translations.idiomatic: Jizhong said to Jilong: "These are elite troops — they should be kept to hold the city; if the enemy comes, who in the city will fight beside the brave?

sentences.zh: 」繼隆不從。

translations.literal: Jilong did not follow this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong would not listen.

sentences.zh: 既而契丹入寇，城陷，卒妻子皆為所俘。

translations.literal: Before long the Khitan invaded; the city fell, and the soldiers' wives and children were all taken captive.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Khitan invaded; the city fell, and the soldiers' wives and children were all taken captive.

sentences.zh: 繼隆疑此卒怨己，欲分隸諸軍。

translations.literal: Jilong suspected these soldiers resented him and wanted to distribute them among various armies.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong suspected these soldiers resented him and wanted to break them up among other units.

sentences.zh: 繼忠曰：「不可，但奏升其軍額，優以廩給，使之盡節可也。

translations.literal: Jizhong said: "That will not do — simply memorialize to raise their army's designation and favor them with generous rations, so that they will give their utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhong said: "That will not do — simply memorialize to raise their army's designation and treat them generously, so that they will give their utmost.

sentences.zh: 」從之，眾皆感悅。

translations.literal: [Jilong] followed this; all were moved and gratified.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong followed his advice, and the men were deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 繼忠因自請以隸麾下。

translations.literal: Jizhong thereupon requested on his own that they be attached to his command.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhong then asked to take them under his own command.

sentences.zh: 會契丹騎大至，駐唐河北，諸將欲堅壁待之。

translations.literal: When Khitan horsemen arrived in great numbers and halted north of the Tang River, the generals wished to hold fast behind walls and wait them out.
translations.idiomatic: When a large Khitan cavalry force arrived and halted north of the Tang River, the generals wanted to hold the walls and wait.

sentences.zh: 繼忠曰：「今強敵在近，城中屯重兵不能剪滅，令長驅深入，侵略他郡，雖欲謀自安之計，豈折衝禦侮之用乎？

translations.literal: Jizhong said: "With a powerful foe close at hand, the city holds a heavy garrison yet cannot destroy them — to let them drive deep inland and ravage other prefectures, even if we seek a plan for our own safety, is that the use of one who repels the foe and guards against insult?
translations.idiomatic: Jizhong said: "With a powerful enemy close at hand, we hold a heavy garrison in the city yet cannot destroy them — to let them drive deep inland and ravage other prefectures, even if we seek our own safety, what use is a force kept to ward off invasion?

sentences.zh: 我將身先士卒，死於寇矣！

translations.literal: I will take the lead among the soldiers and die fighting the raiders!
translations.idiomatic: I will lead the soldiers myself and die fighting the enemy!

sentences.zh: 」辭氣慷慨，眾壯之。

translations.literal: His words were ardent and generous; the crowd was emboldened.
translations.idiomatic: His words were fierce and resolute, and the men took heart.

sentences.zh: 靜塞軍摧鋒先入，契丹兵大潰。

translations.literal: The Jingse Army smashed the enemy vanguard and entered first; the Khitan army routed completely.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingse Army smashed the enemy vanguard and went in first; the Khitan army broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞之，降璽書獎諭，賜予甚厚。

translations.literal: When Taizong heard of it, he issued an imperial edict of commendation; the gifts granted were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong heard of it, he sent down an imperial edict of commendation and rewarded him very generously.

sentences.zh: 淳化初，遷引進使，護鎮定、高陽關兩路屯兵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chunhua he was transferred to introducing commissioner and guarded the garrison troops on the two routes of Zhending and Gaoyang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Chunhua era he was promoted to introducing commissioner and put in charge of the garrison troops on the Zhending and Gaoyang Pass routes.

sentences.zh: 三年，被病，召赴闕，卒，年五十五。

translations.literal: In the third year he fell ill, was summoned to court, and died at age fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he fell ill, was summoned to court, and died at the age of fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 繼忠長厚忠謹，士大夫多與遊，前後賜賚鉅萬計，悉以犒賞士卒。

translations.literal: Jizhong was generous, loyal, and careful; many scholar-officials kept company with him; gifts from the throne totaling tens of thousands he gave entirely to reward his soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhong was generous, loyal, and conscientious; many scholar-officials sought his company, and the imperial gifts he received over the years, totaling tens of thousands, he gave entirely to reward his soldiers.

sentences.zh: 身死之日，家無餘財，搢紳稱之。

translations.literal: On the day he died his household had no surplus wealth; the gentry praised him for it.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he died his household had no wealth left, and the gentry praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 子用成，雍熙初登進士第，至太常博士。

translations.literal: His son Yongcheng passed the jinshi examination at the beginning of Yongxi and rose to erudite of the Grand Academy of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yongcheng passed the jinshi examination at the beginning of the Yongxi era and rose to erudite of the Grand Academy of Rites.

sentences.zh: 崔彥進

translations.literal: Cui Yanjin
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yanjin

sentences.zh: 崔彥進，大名人。

translations.literal: Cui Yanjin was a native of Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yanjin was a native of Daming.

sentences.zh: 純質有膽略，善騎射。

translations.literal: Plain and honest in character, he had courage and strategic sense and was skilled at horseback archery.
translations.idiomatic: Plain and honest by nature, he had courage and strategic sense and was skilled at mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐中，隸周祖帳下。

translations.literal: During the Qianyou era of Han he served under the Zhou founder.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianyou era of Han he served under the Zhou founder.

sentences.zh: 廣順初，補衛士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun he was appointed an imperial guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Guangshun era he was appointed an imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 世宗鎮澶淵，令領禁兵以從。

translations.literal: When Shizong was posted at Chanyuan he was ordered to lead palace troops to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong was posted at Chanyuan, he was ordered to lead palace troops in his retinue.

sentences.zh: 顯德初，為控鶴指揮使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande he became commander of the Crane Controllers.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xiande era he became commander of the Crane Controllers.

sentences.zh: 從征淮南，以功遷散員都虞候。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Huainan and was promoted to overall adjutant of the miscellaneous ranks for merit.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the campaign against Huainan and was promoted to overall adjutant of the miscellaneous ranks for his achievements.

sentences.zh: 從平瓦橋關，改東西班指揮使、領昭州刺史。

translations.literal: He followed the pacification of Waqiao Pass and was made commander of the Eastern and Western Banners, concurrently given Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the pacification of Waqiao Pass and was made commander of the Eastern and Western Banners, with Zhao Prefecture added to his command.

sentences.zh: 宋初，改控鶴右廂指揮使、領果州團練使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was made commander of the Right Wing of the Crane Controllers, concurrently given Guo Prefecture as training commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Song he was made commander of the Right Wing of the Crane Controllers and given Guo Prefecture as training commissioner.

sentences.zh: 征李筠，為先鋒部署，以功遷常州防禦使。

translations.literal: In the campaign against Li Yun he served as vanguard commander and was promoted to defense commissioner of Changzhou for merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Li Yun he served as vanguard commander and was promoted to defense commissioner of Changzhou for his achievements.

sentences.zh: 從平李重進，改虎捷右廂。

translations.literal: He followed the pacification of Li Chongjin and was transferred to the Right Wing of the Tiger Raiders.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the pacification of Li Chongjin and was transferred to the Right Wing of the Tiger Raiders.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年，遷侍衛步軍都指揮使、領武信軍節度。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianlong he was promoted to overall commander of the Palace Foot Army, concurrently given command of the Wuxin military governorship.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianlong 2 he was promoted to overall commander of the Palace Foot Army and given command of the Wuxin military governorship.

sentences.zh: 大舉伐蜀，為鳳州路行營前軍副都部署。

translations.literal: In the great campaign against Shu he was deputy overall commander of the vanguard on the Fengzhou route expedition headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the great campaign against Shu he served as deputy overall commander of the vanguard on the Fengzhou route expedition headquarters.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，坐縱部下略玉帛、子女及諸不法事，左遷昭化軍節度觀察留後。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified he was demoted for allowing his subordinates to plunder silks, money, women, and children and for various unlawful acts, to acting military governor and observation commissioner of the Zhaohua Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu was pacified he was demoted for allowing his men to plunder silks, money, women, and children and for other unlawful acts, to acting military governor and observation commissioner of the Zhaohua Army.

sentences.zh: 太祖郊祀西洛，彥進來朝，授彰信軍節度。

translations.literal: When Taizu performed suburban sacrifice at Luoyang, Yanjin came to court and was given the Zhangxin military governorship.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu performed the suburban sacrifice at Luoyang, Yanjin came to court and was given the Zhangxin military governorship.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，移鎮河陽。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo he was transferred to govern Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 2 he was transferred to govern Heyang.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，遣將征太原，分命攻城，以彥進與郢州防禦使尹勳攻其東，彰德軍節度李漢瓊、冀州刺史牛思進攻其南，桂州觀察使曹翰、翰林使杜彥圭攻其西，彰信軍節度劉遇、光州刺史史珪攻其北。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year generals were dispatched to campaign against Taiyuan; the assault on the city was divided by assignment: Yanjin together with Yingzhou defense commissioner Yin Xun attacked the east; Zhangde Army military governor Li Hanqiong and Jizhou prefect Niu Sijin attacked the south; Guizhou observation commissioner Cao Han and Hanlin commissioner Du Yangui attacked the west; Zhangxin Army military governor Liu Yu and Guangzhou prefect Shi Gui attacked the north.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year generals were sent to campaign against Taiyuan, and the siege was divided among them: Yanjin and Yingzhou Defense Commissioner Yin Xun attacked the east; Zhangde Army Military Governor Li Hanqiong and Jizhou Prefect Niu Sijin the south; Guizhou Observation Commissioner Cao Han and Hanlin Commissioner Du Yangui the west; and Zhangxin Army Military Governor Liu Yu and Guangzhou Prefect Shi Gui the north.

sentences.zh: 彥進督戰甚急，太祖嘉之。

translations.literal: Yanjin pressed the attack very hard, and Taizu commended him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjin pressed the attack very hard, and Taizu commended him for it.

sentences.zh: 晉陽平，從征幽州，又與內供奉官江守鈞率兵攻城之西北。

translations.literal: When Jinyang was pacified he followed the campaign against Youzhou and again with palace attendant Jiang Shoujun led troops to assault the northwest of the city.
translations.idiomatic: After Jinyang fell he joined the campaign against Youzhou and again led troops with Palace Attendant Jiang Shoujun to assault the northwest of the city.

sentences.zh: 及班師，詔彥進與西上閤門副使薛繼興、閤門祗候李守斌領兵屯關南，以功加檢校太尉。

translations.literal: When the army returned, an edict ordered Yanjin together with vice commissioner of the Western Upper Gate Xue Jixing and gate attendant Li Shoubin to lead troops garrisoned at Guannan; for merit he was given the additional title of grand marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, Yanjin was ordered with Vice Commissioner of the Western Upper Gate Xue Jixing and Gate Attendant Li Shoubin to lead troops garrisoned at Guannan, and for his achievements he was given the additional title of grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 是秋，契丹侵遂城，彥進與劉廷翰、崔翰等擊破之，斬首萬級。

translations.literal: That autumn the Khitan invaded Suicheng; Yanjin together with Liu Tinghan, Cui Han, and others defeated them and took ten thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the Khitan invaded Suicheng; Yanjin, Liu Tinghan, Cui Han, and others routed them and took ten thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 五年，車駕北巡，以彥進為關南都部署，敗契丹於唐興口。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the emperor toured north; Yanjin was made overall commander of Guannan and defeated the Khitan at Tangxingkou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the emperor toured the north; Yanjin was made overall commander of Guannan and defeated the Khitan at Tangxingkou.

sentences.zh: 彥進頻立戰功，然好聚財貨，所至無善政。

translations.literal: Yanjin repeatedly won battlefield glory, yet he loved to amass wealth; wherever he went he left no good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjin won battlefield glory again and again, yet he loved to amass wealth, and wherever he was posted he left no record of good governance.

sentences.zh: 沒後，諸子爭家財，有司攝治。

translations.literal: After his death his sons fought over the family wealth, and the authorities intervened to settle it.
translations.idiomatic: After his death his sons quarreled over the family wealth, and the authorities stepped in to settle the dispute.

sentences.zh: 太宗召見，為決之，謂左右曰：「此細務，朕不宜親臨，但以彥進嘗任節制，不欲令其子辱於父耳。」

translations.literal: Taizong summoned them, decided the matter for them, and said to those beside him: "This is a petty affair — I ought not to attend to it in person; it is only because Yanjin once held a military governorship that I do not wish his sons to bring shame upon their father."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong summoned them and settled the matter himself, then said to those beside him: "This is a petty affair and I ought not to attend to it in person; I am doing so only because Yanjin once held a military governorship, and I do not wish his sons to bring shame upon their father."

sentences.zh: 子懷遵，至內殿崇班；

translations.literal: His son Huaizun rose to honored rank of the Inner Hall;
translations.idiomatic: His son Huaizun rose to honored rank of the Inner Hall;

sentences.zh: 懷清，至崇儀副使。

translations.literal: Huaqing rose to vice commissioner of honored ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Huaqing rose to vice commissioner of honored ceremony.

sentences.zh: 懷遵子上賢，娶鎮王女崇安縣主。

translations.literal: Huaizun's son Shangxian married the Princess of Chong'an, daughter of the Prince of Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizun's son Shangxian married the Princess of Chong'an, daughter of the Prince of Zhen.

sentences.zh: 懷清子從湜，娶岐王女永壽縣主，為西京左藏庫副使，後坐事除名。

translations.literal: Huaqing's son Congshi married the Princess of Yongshou, daughter of the Prince of Qi; he served as vice commissioner of the Western Capital Left Repository and later was stripped of his name for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Huaqing's son Congshi married the Princess of Yongshou, daughter of the Prince of Qi; he served as vice commissioner of the Western Capital Left Repository and was later stripped of rank for an offense.

sentences.zh: 張廷翰

translations.literal: Zhang Tinghan
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tinghan

sentences.zh: 張廷翰，澤州陵川人。

translations.literal: Zhang Tinghan was a native of Lingchuan in Ze Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tinghan was a native of Lingchuan in Ze Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初為漢祖親校。

translations.literal: At first he was a personal guard of the Han founder.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a personal guard of the Han founder.

sentences.zh: 漢祖入汴，補內殿直，遷東西班軍使。

translations.literal: When the Han founder entered Bian he was appointed to the Inner Hall Direct and was promoted to army commander of the Eastern and Western Banners.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han founder entered Bian he was appointed to the Inner Hall Direct and was promoted to army commander of the Eastern and Western Banners.

sentences.zh: 周初，改護聖指揮使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhou he was made commander of the Sacred Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhou he was made commander of the Sacred Guard.

sentences.zh: 從世宗平淮甸，以功遷鐵騎右第二軍都虞候。

translations.literal: He followed Shizong in pacifying the Huai region and was promoted to overall adjutant of the Second Army of the Right Iron Cavalry for merit.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Shizong in pacifying the Huai region and was promoted to overall adjutant of the Second Army of the Right Iron Cavalry for his achievements.

sentences.zh: 顯德末，改殿前散都頭都虞候。

translations.literal: At the end of Xiande he was made overall adjutant of the miscellaneous company heads of the Palace Front.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Xiande era he was made overall adjutant of the miscellaneous company heads of the Palace Front.

sentences.zh: 宋初，權為鐵騎左第二軍都校、領開州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was acting commander of the Second Army of the Left Iron Cavalry, concurrently given Kai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Song he was acting commander of the Second Army of the Left Iron Cavalry and given Kai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 從平揚州，又以功遷控鶴左廂都指揮使、領果州團練使。
