translations.literal: He followed the pacification of Yangzhou and again for merit was promoted to overall commander of the Left Wing of the Crane Controllers, concurrently given Guo Prefecture as training commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the pacification of Yangzhou and was again promoted for his achievements to overall commander of the Left Wing of the Crane Controllers, with Guo Prefecture as training commissioner.

sentences.zh: 未幾，轉龍捷左廂都指揮使、領春州團練使。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to overall commander of the Left Wing of the Dragon Raiders, concurrently given Chun Prefecture as training commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to overall commander of the Left Wing of the Dragon Raiders, with Chun Prefecture as training commissioner.

sentences.zh: 乾德中，興師伐蜀，以廷翰為歸州路行營馬軍都指揮使，隨劉廷讓由歸州路進討。

translations.literal: During Qiande troops were raised to campaign against Shu; Tinghan was made overall commander of the cavalry on the Guizhou route expedition headquarters and followed Liu Tingrang in advancing by the Guizhou route.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qiande era the court raised an army against Shu; Tinghan was made overall commander of the cavalry on the Guizhou route expedition headquarters and advanced with Liu Tingrang by the Guizhou route.

sentences.zh: 師次夔州，廷讓頓兵白帝廟西，俄而夔州監軍武守謙率所部來拒戰，廷翰引兵逆擊，敗之於豬頭鋪，乘勝拔其城。

translations.literal: When the army halted at Kuizhou, Tingrang encamped west of the White Emperor Shrine; before long Kuizhou army inspector Wu Shouqian led his troops to offer battle; Tinghan led troops to meet the attack, defeated them at Zhutou Post, and pressed the victory to take the city.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Kuizhou, Tingrang encamped west of the White Emperor Shrine; before long Kuizhou Army Inspector Wu Shouqian led his troops out to fight; Tinghan met the attack, defeated them at Zhutou Post, and pressed the victory to capture the city.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，授侍衛馬步軍都虞候、領彰國軍節度。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified he was given the post of overall adjutant of the Palace Horse and Foot Army, concurrently given the Zhangguo military governorship.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu was pacified he was made overall adjutant of the Palace Horse and Foot Army and given the Zhangguo military governorship.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，寢疾，太祖親臨問，未幾卒，年五十三。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaibao he fell ill in bed; Taizu came in person to inquire after him; before long he died at age fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaibao 2 he took to his bed with illness; Taizu came in person to inquire after him, and before long he died at the age of fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the title of palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously given the title of palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 皇甫繼明

translations.literal: Huangfu Jiming
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Jiming

sentences.zh: 皇甫繼明，冀州蓨人。

translations.literal: Huangfu Jiming was a native of Tiao in Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Jiming was a native of Tiao in Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父濟，汾川令。

translations.literal: His father Ji was magistrate of Fenchuan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ji was magistrate of Fenchuan.

sentences.zh: 繼明身長七尺，善騎射，以膂力聞郡中。

translations.literal: Jiming stood seven feet tall, was skilled at horseback archery, and was known throughout the commandery for his physical strength.
translations.idiomatic: Jiming stood seven feet tall, was skilled at mounted archery, and was known throughout the commandery for his physical strength.

sentences.zh: 刺史張廷翰以隸左右，薦於太祖，補殿前指揮使，歷左右番押班都知。

translations.literal: Prefect Zhang Tinghan took him into his personal staff and recommended him to Taizu; he was appointed a commander of the Palace Front and served successively as overall director of the left and right rotating guard shifts.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Zhang Tinghan took him into his personal staff and recommended him to Taizu; he was appointed a commander of the Palace Front and served successively as overall director of the left and right rotating guard shifts.

sentences.zh: 至道元年，改領洋州觀察使，充環慶路馬步軍都部署，繼明謹愿，御下嚴肅，士卒頗畏憚之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhidao he was transferred to observation commissioner of Yang Prefecture and appointed overall commander of the horse and foot forces on the Huanqing route; Jiming was careful and sincere, strict in commanding subordinates, and the soldiers greatly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhidao 1 he was transferred to observation commissioner of Yang Prefecture and appointed overall commander of the horse and foot forces on the Huanqing route; Jiming was careful and sincere, strict with his men, and the soldiers greatly feared him.

sentences.zh: 二年，受詔護送輜重赴靈州，繼明已先約靈州部署田紹斌率軍迎援，適被病，裨將白守榮謂繼明曰：「君疾甚，不可行，恐失期會，守榮當率兵先往。

translations.literal: In the second year he received an edict to escort baggage trains to Lingzhou; Jiming had already arranged for Lingzhou commander Tian Shaobin to lead troops to meet and reinforce him; just then he fell ill, and vice general Bai Shourong said to Jiming: "Your illness is severe — you cannot travel; we may miss the rendezvous; Shourong will lead the troops ahead.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he received orders to escort baggage trains to Lingzhou; Jiming had already arranged for Lingzhou Commander Tian Shaobin to lead troops to meet and reinforce him, but he then fell ill, and Vice General Bai Shourong said to him: "Your illness is severe — you cannot travel; we may miss the rendezvous; I will lead the troops ahead.

sentences.zh: 」繼明宿將，慮守榮等輕佻，與戎人接戰，因謂之曰：「我疾少間。

translations.literal: Jiming was a veteran general and feared that Shourong and the others were frivolous in fighting the barbarians; he therefore said to them: "My illness has eased somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Jiming was a veteran general and feared that Shourong and the others would be reckless in fighting the barbarians, so he said to them: "My illness has eased somewhat.

sentences.zh: 」遂矍鑠被甲上馬，強行至清遠軍，卒，年六十三，詔贈彰武軍節度。

translations.literal: He then vigrously donned armor, mounted his horse, and forced his way as far as the Qingyuan Army, where he died at age sixty-three; an edict posthumously gave him the Zhangwu military governorship.
translations.idiomatic: He then roused himself, donned armor, mounted his horse, and forced his way as far as Qingyuan Army, where he died at the age of sixty-three; an edict posthumously gave him the Zhangwu military governorship.

sentences.zh: 遷其子懷信為供奉官。

translations.literal: His son Huaixin was promoted to palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huaixin was promoted to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 張瓊，大名館陶人。

translations.literal: Zhang Qiong was a native of Guantao in Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qiong was a native of Guantao in Daming.

sentences.zh: 世為牙中軍。

translations.literal: For generations his family served in the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his family had served in the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 瓊少有勇力，善射，隸太祖帳下。

translations.literal: Qiong in youth had courage and strength, was skilled at archery, and served under Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong had courage and strength from youth, was skilled at archery, and served under Taizu.

sentences.zh: 周顯德中，太祖從世宗南征，擊十八里灘砦，為戰艦所圍，一人甲盾鼓噪而前，眾莫敢當，太祖命瓊射之，一發而踣，淮人遂卻。

translations.literal: During the Xiande era of Zhou, Taizu followed Shizong on the southern campaign and attacked the fort at Shibalitan; he was surrounded by warships; one man in armor and shield came forward with a clamor, and none dared meet him; Taizu ordered Qiong to shoot him; with one shot he fell, and the Huai men then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiande era of Zhou, Taizu followed Shizong on the southern campaign and attacked the fort at Shibalitan; warships surrounded them; one man in armor and shield came forward shouting, and none dared meet him; Taizu ordered Qiong to shoot, and with one shot the man fell; the Huai men then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 瓊性暴無機，多所淩轢。

translations.literal: Qiong was violent by nature and lacked tact; he bullied many people.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong was violent by nature and lacked tact, and he bullied many people.

sentences.zh: 時史珪、石漢卿方用事，瓊輕侮之，目為巫媼。

translations.literal: At the time Shi Gui and Shi Hanqing were in power; Qiong treated them with contempt and called them old witches.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Shi Gui and Shi Hanqing were in power, but Qiong treated them with contempt and called them old witches.

sentences.zh: 二人銜之切齒，發瓊擅乘官馬，納李筠隸僕，畜部曲百餘人，恣作威福，禁軍皆懼；

translations.literal: The two men hated him to the teeth; they reported that Qiong had usurped official horses, taken Li Yun's bond servants, kept more than a hundred retainers, and abused his power at will; the palace troops all feared him;
translations.idiomatic: The two men hated him bitterly; they reported that Qiong had usurped official horses, taken Li Yun's bond servants, kept more than a hundred retainers, and abused his power at will, and the palace troops all feared him;

sentences.zh: 又誣毀太宗為殿前都虞候時事。

translations.literal: They also slandered matters from when Taizong had been overall adjutant of the Palace Front.
translations.idiomatic: They also slandered matters from when Taizong had served as overall adjutant of the Palace Front.

sentences.zh: 建隆四年秋，郊禋制下，方欲肅靜京師，乃召訊瓊。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fourth year of Jianlong the suburban sacrifice regulations were issued; the court was just then seeking to quiet the capital, and Qiong was summoned for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Jianlong 4 the suburban sacrifice regulations were issued; the court was seeking to quiet the capital, and Qiong was summoned for interrogation.

sentences.zh: 瓊不伏，太祖怒，令擊之。

translations.literal: Qiong would not confess; Taizu was angry and ordered him beaten.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong would not confess; Taizu was angry and ordered him beaten.

sentences.zh: 漢卿即奮鐵撾亂下，氣垂絕，曳出，遂下御史案鞫之。

translations.literal: Hanqing immediately swung an iron mace and struck him repeatedly; his breath was nearly gone; he was dragged out, and the case was sent down to the censorate for trial.
translations.idiomatic: Hanqing immediately swung an iron mace and struck him repeatedly until he was nearly dead; he was dragged out, and the case was sent to the censorate for trial.

sentences.zh: 瓊知不免，行至明德門，解所係繫帶以遺母。

translations.literal: Qiong knew he could not escape; reaching the Gate of Bright Virtue he untied the belt he was bound with and gave it to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong knew he could not escape; reaching the Gate of Bright Virtue he untied the belt he was bound with and gave it to his mother.

sentences.zh: 獄具，賜死於城西井亭。

translations.literal: When the case was complete he was granted death at the well pavilion west of the city.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was complete he was granted death at the well pavilion west of the city.

sentences.zh: 太祖旋聞家無餘財，止有僕三人，甚悔之。

translations.literal: Taizu soon heard that the household had no surplus wealth and only three servants, and deeply regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu soon learned that the household had no wealth left and only three servants, and deeply regretted it.

sentences.zh: 因責漢卿曰：「汝言瓊有僕百人，今何在？

translations.literal: He therefore rebuked Hanqing, saying: "You said Qiong had a hundred servants — where are they now?
translations.idiomatic: He therefore rebuked Hanqing, saying: "You said Qiong had a hundred servants — where are they now?

sentences.zh: 」漢卿曰：「瓊所養者一敵百耳。

translations.literal: Hanqing said: "The men Qiong kept were each worth a hundred ordinary men."
translations.idiomatic: Hanqing said: "The men Qiong kept were each worth a hundred ordinary men."

sentences.zh: 」太祖遂優恤其家。

translations.literal: Taizu then treated his family with generous relief.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu then treated his family with generous relief.

sentences.zh: 以其子尚幼，乃擢其兄進為龍捷副指揮使。

translations.literal: Because his son was still young, his elder brother Jin was promoted to vice commander of the Dragon Raiders.
translations.idiomatic: Because his son was still young, his elder brother Jin was promoted to vice commander of the Dragon Raiders.

sentences.zh: 論曰：崔彥進與王全斌征蜀，黷貨殺降，以致蜀亂，惟劉廷讓一軍秋毫無犯，紀律嚴否於斯別矣。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Cui Yanjin and Wang Quanbin campaigned against Shu, took bribes and killed those who surrendered, and thereby brought on the Shu rebellion; only Liu Tingrang's army did not violate so much as a hair — whether discipline was strict or lax is here clearly distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal says: Cui Yanjin and Wang Quanbin campaigned against Shu, took bribes and killed those who surrendered, and thereby brought on the Shu rebellion; only Liu Tingrang's army did not violate so much as a hair — the difference between strict and lax discipline could not be clearer.

sentences.zh: 尹崇珂斤斤謹厚，臨淄攻守之績，嶺嶠廓清之勞，至於瘁事。

translations.literal: Yin Chongke was scrupulously careful and generous; his achievements in attack and defense at Linzi and his labor in clearing the Lingjiao region wore him out in service.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Chongke was scrupulously careful and generous; his achievements in attack and defense at Linzi and his labor in clearing the Lingjiao region wore him out in service.

sentences.zh: 皇甫繼明力疾以護軍行，純誠勇節，皆足嘉尚。

translations.literal: Huangfu Jiming forced himself onward despite illness to guard the army on the march; his pure loyalty and courageous integrity are all worthy of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Jiming forced himself onward despite illness to guard the army on the march; his pure loyalty and courageous integrity are all worthy of praise.

sentences.zh: 張廷翰西征，未睹奇效。

translations.literal: Zhang Tinghan on the western campaign showed no marked extraordinary achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tinghan's western campaign showed no marked extraordinary achievement.

sentences.zh: 張美雖稱幹敏，而初有自愧之行。

translations.literal: Zhang Mei, though called capable and quick, at first had conduct that made him ashamed of himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mei, though called capable and quick, at first had conduct that made him ashamed of himself.

sentences.zh: 郭守文敦詩閱禮，輕財好施，慎保封疆，士卒樂用，終以勳舊蒙眷，聯姻戚里。

translations.literal: Guo Shuowen was steeped in the classics and versed in ritual, lightly valued wealth and loved to give, carefully guarded the frontier, and his soldiers were glad to serve under him; in the end as an old meritorious servant he won favor and married into the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Shuowen was steeped in the classics and versed in ritual, lightly valued wealth and loved to give, carefully guarded the frontier, and his soldiers were glad to serve under him; in the end, as an old meritorious servant, he won favor and married into the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 宋初諸將，要終而論，臧否異趣，何昭昭若是哉！

translations.literal: Among the generals at the beginning of Song, taking their lives as a whole to judge them, praise and blame diverge in so many directions — how plainly evident this is!
translations.idiomatic: Among the generals of early Song, judged by their lives as a whole, praise and blame diverge in so many directions — how plainly evident this is!
